audit_findings.title: Parent-common owner earnings may contain noncontrolling-interest cash flows
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable income is combined with consolidated D&A, maintenance capital, working-capital items, and potentially cash; these affect OE and the equity bridge before division by parent common shares.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company's 65 % ownership of Skyland's equity resulted in the consolidation of Skyland’s results in the Company's Consolidated Financial Statements in the Agribusiness segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter inconsistency is demonstrated: Skyland is only 65% owned, yet it is consolidated. The net valuation error remains unresolved because subsidiary-level add-backs and deductions were not supplied. Materiality is reasonably possible: filed 2025 NCI income was $23.588 million, 31.7% of the $74.4 million anchor, although that amount is not itself the OE error. Full D&A can overstate OE, while full capital and working-capital deductions can understate it; consolidated cash can overstate the bridge.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile D&A, maintenance capital, working capital, and bridge assets by subsidiary and ownership percentage for every OE year, then rerun using parent-only amounts or deduct an explicitly valued NCI claim from a consistently consolidated valuation.

audit_findings.title: A temporary Section 45Z credit may have been capitalized into perpetuity
audit_findings.magnitude: $34.986 million in FY2025, equal to 47.0% of the $74.4 million anchor; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The temporary credit enters owner earnings through other income and is then grown and included in terminal earnings despite its statutory 2029 expiration.
audit_findings.evidence: On July 4, 2025, the credit was extended through 2029 under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated horizon error if the supplied anchor retains the filed credit, as the valuation contains no sunset adjustment. The credit is nearly half the anchor, and the terminal value represents 46.3%-50.9% of operating PV. The additional $50.390 million recognized in the first half of 2026 confirms current significance but does not support earnings after 2029.
audit_findings.action: Separate Section 45Z from recurring OE, model eligible and collectible credits only through 2029 with monetization and compliance adjustments, remove the credit from terminal earnings, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor does not represent the current TAMH ownership perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 parent earnings anchor reflects 50.1% ownership for seven months and 100% thereafter, while forecast value belongs to the current 100%-owned parent claim.
audit_findings.evidence: We acquired 100% of our ethanol plants at the end of July, which generated nearly $40 million of incremental plant income before income taxes attributable to the company in the back half of the year.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because no perimeter adjustment was made. The filing reports nearly $40 million of incremental plant income before tax attributable to the company during the post-acquisition half of 2025, showing a scale capable of materially affecting a $74.4 million OE anchor. That $40 million is not the missing pro-forma OE amount because taxes, interest, maintenance capital, timing, and former NCI allocation remain unreconciled.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a parent-common pro-forma FY2025 OE statement as though TAMH were wholly owned from January 1, including taxes, incremental financing cost, maintenance capital, working capital, and elimination of the former NCI allocation; then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Incident-related insurance income may be embedded as recurring earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $27.002 million of FY2025 property-insurance recoveries plus $1.4 million of business-interruption recoveries; net normalization unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Insurance recoveries increase the OE anchor, while related impairment, repair costs, lost operations, and replacement capital can offset or reverse the adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: The vast majority of the property insurance recoveries recorded in 2025 are related to a current year incident at a grain terminal in Sunray, Texas.
audit_findings.explanation: The incident and recoveries are demonstrated, but the net OE error is unresolved because the supplied record does not show whether the valuation removed them or consistently treated the related $14.777 million Agribusiness impairment and other incident costs. The $27.002 million property recovery alone equals 36.3% of the anchor, making the unresolved normalization reasonably capable of changing value.
audit_findings.action: Trace each Sunray-related recovery into OE and reconcile it with impairment, business-interruption loss, repairs, replacement capital, and receivables; retain only recurring operating economics and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor tax burden includes a nonrecurring reserve reversal
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.580 million FY2025 tax benefit, equal to 11.5% of the $74.4 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The reserve reversal reduces the tax provision and raises parent net income feeding OE; leaving it in the anchor causes a discrete benefit to grow through the forecast and terminal period.
audit_findings.evidence: The difference between the 15.7% effective tax rate and the U.S. federal statutory tax rate of 21% is primarily attributable to the tax impact of noncontrolling interest, nontaxable clean fuel production credits and the reversal of certain unrecognized tax benefits, partially offset by state and local taxes, nondeductible compensation, and valuation allowances on losses in foreign tax jurisdictions.
audit_findings.explanation: The reversal is demonstrated by the filed effective-tax-rate reconciliation. It is not evidence of a sustainable future cash-tax reduction. At 11.5% of anchor OE, it is material to intrinsic value and the buy-below threshold even though removing it would reinforce, rather than reverse, the present conclusion that the $69.31 market price exceeds all stated scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Remove the $8.580 million discrete benefit, separately reconcile associated interest and settlements, derive a sustainable parent-only cash-tax rate excluding NCI and temporary Section 45Z effects, and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating liquidity rather than distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $66.549 million maximum bridge exposure, equal to $1.89 per share and 5.9% of $1.125 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for inventory funding, derivative margin, restricted subsidiaries, or NCI cannot be distributed and should not be added to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, periods of high grain prices could require us to make additional margin deposits on our exchange traded futures contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating-liquidity requirement is demonstrated qualitatively, but the amount of nonsurplus cash is unresolved. Even treating the entire $66.549 million balance as unavailable would reduce base value from $31.98 to approximately $30.09 per share, still 56.6% below the $69.31 market price. Thus this item alone cannot change the stated valuation conclusion, although it can modestly reduce the bridge and buy-below figure.
audit_findings.action: Establish minimum through-cycle operating and margin liquidity, identify restricted and NCI-owned cash, and replace the bridge amount with demonstrably parent-owned surplus cash; no conclusion-changing rerun is required unless additional cash-like assets or restrictions are identified.
